tasks.title: Super massive black hole mean mass density
tasks.statement: Calculate the mean mass density for a super massive black hole with total mass of 1×108 M⨀ inside the Schwarzschild radius.

parts.question: Calculate the mean mass density for a super massive black hole with total mass of 1×108 M⨀ inside the Schwarzschild radius.
parts.reference: The Schwarzschild radius is given by R = 2GM/c^2. The mean density is rho = M / ((4/3)*pi*R^3) = 3c^6 / (32 * pi * G^2 * M^2). Substituting the values, rho = 1.85 * 10^3 kg m^-3.

tasks.title: Photons from G2 star
tasks.statement: Estimate the number of photons per second that arrive on our eye at λ = 550 nm (V-band) from a G2 main sequence star with apparent magnitude of m = 6 (the threshold of naked eye visibility). Assume the eye pupil diameter is 6 mm and all the radition from this star is in λ = 550 nm.

parts.question: Estimate the number of photons per second that arrive on our eye at λ = 550 nm from a G2 main sequence star with apparent magnitude m = 6, assuming eye pupil diameter 6 mm.
parts.reference: m_1 - m_2 = -2.5 log(F_1 / F_2); 6 - (-26.8) = -2.5 log(F_1 / (1.37 * 10^3)); F_1 = 1.04 * 10^-11 W/m^2. Energy of one photon E_ph = hc/lambda = 3.62 * 10^-19 J. Number of photons = (F_1 * pi * (d/2)^2) / E_ph = 8 * 10^3 photons per second.

tasks.title: Planet radius for vertical jump escape
tasks.statement: Estimate the radius of a planet that a man can escape its gravitation by jumping vertically. Assume density of the planet and the Earth are the same.

parts.question: Estimate the radius of a planet that a man can escape its gravitation by jumping vertically, assuming same density as Earth.
parts.reference: v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 0.5) = 3.13 m/s. Escape velocity v = sqrt(2GM/R) = sqrt((8/3)*pi*G*rho*R^2). R = 3v / sqrt(8*pi*G*rho) = 2 * 10^6 m (2000 km).

tasks.title: Tabeshband architecture
tasks.statement: In a typical Persian architecture, on top of south side windows there is a structure called "Tabeshband" (shader), which controls sunlight in summer and winter. In summer when the Sun is high, Tabeshband prevents sunlight to enter rooms and keeps inside cooler. In the modern architecture it is verified that the Tabeshband saves about 20% of energy cost. Figure (1) shows a vertical section of this design at latitude of 36.0° N with window and Tabeshband. Using the parameters given in the figure, calculate the maximum width of the Tabeshband, "𝑥", and maximum height of the window , "ℎ" in such a way that: i) No direct sunlight can enter to the room in the summer solstice at noon. ii) The direct sunlight reaches the end of the room (indicated by the point A in the figure) in the winter solstice at noon.

parts.question: Calculate the maximum width of the Tabeshband 'x' and maximum height of the window 'h' satisfying the summer and winter solstice conditions.
parts.reference: Summer solstice noon sun altitude: theta_S = 90 - 36 + 23.5 = 77.5°. Winter solstice noon sun altitude: theta_W = 90 - 36 - 23.5 = 30.5°. From geometry: tan(theta_S) = y/h = 0.22, tan(theta_W) = (y+h)/x = 1.70. Solving gives y = 0.80 m, h = 3.7 m (or h = 3.7 m, x = 2.7 m depending on diagram parameters, standard solution h = 3.7 m).

tasks.title: Damavand mountain circumpolar star declination
tasks.statement: The Damavand Mountain is located at the North part of Iran, in south coast of Caspian Sea. Consider an observer standing on the Damavand mountaintop (latitude = 35° 57′ N; longitude = 52° 6' E; altitude 5.6 × 10^3 m from the mean sea level) and looking at the sky over the Caspian Sea. What is the minimum declination for a star, to be seen marginally circumpolar for this observer. Geodetic radius of the Earth at this latitude is 6370.8 km. Surface level of the Caspian Sea is approximately equal to the mean sea level.

parts.question: What is the minimum declination for a star to be seen marginally circumpolar for this observer on Damavand mountain?
parts.reference: Cos(beta) = R / (R + h) => beta = 2° 24'. Refraction at horizon = 34'. Minimum declination delta_min = 90 - phi - R_ref - beta = 90 - 35° 57' - 34' - 2° 24' = 51° 5'.

tasks.title: Escape velocity from center of proto-star cloud
tasks.statement: Derive a relation for the escape velocity of an object, launched from the center of a proto-star cloud. The cloud has uniform density with the mass of M and radius R. Ignore collisions between the particles of the cloud and the launched object. If the object were allowed to fall freely from the surface, it would reach the center with a velocity equal to GM/R.

parts.question: Derive a relation for the escape velocity of an object launched from the center of a uniform proto-star cloud of mass M and radius R.
parts.reference: Using potential inside a uniform sphere and total energy conservation U(0) + (1/2)m v_esc^2 = 0. Potential at center U(0) = -3GM^2 / (2R). Thus v_esc = sqrt(3GM / R).

tasks.title: Field of view of telescope using Vega
tasks.statement: A student tries to measure field of view (FOV) of the eyepiece of his/her telescope, using rotation of the Earth. To do this job, the observer points the telescope towards Vega (alpha Lyr., RA: 18.5h , Dec: +39° ), turns off its "clock drive" and measures trace out time, t=5.3 minutes, that Vega crosses the full diameter of the FOV. What is the FOV of this telescope in arc-minutes?

parts.question: What is the FOV of this telescope in arc-minutes?
parts.reference: Earth rotation speed omega = 2*pi / 86164 = 7.29 * 10^-5 rad/s. Delta_theta = omega * t = 7.29 * 10^-5 * 5.3 * 60 = 0.023 rad. FOV = Delta_theta * cos(Dec) = 0.023 * cos(39°) = 0.018 rad = 62 arc-minutes.

tasks.title: Globular cluster mass
tasks.statement: Estimate the mass of a globular cluster with the radius of r = 20 pc and root mean square velocity of stars equal to v_rms = 3 km s^-1.

parts.question: Estimate the mass of a globular cluster with r = 20 pc and v_rms = 3 km/s.

tasks.title: Star distance from galactic center
tasks.statement: The Galactic longitude of a star is l = 15°. Its radial velocity with respect to the Sun is V_r = 100 km s^-1. Assume stars in the disk of the Galaxy are orbiting the center with a constant velocity of V_0 = 250 km s^-1 in circular orbits in the same sense in the galactic plane. Calculate distance of the star from the center of the Galaxy.

parts.question: Calculate the distance of the star from the center of the Galaxy.
parts.reference: V_r = (V/R - V_0/R_0) * R_0 * sin(l) etc. Using Oort constants or differential rotation relations, R = 8 kpc * V_0 * sin(l) / (V_r + V_0 * sin(l)) yielding R = 5 kpc.

tasks.title: Magnetic field evolution to neutron star
tasks.statement: A main sequence star with the radius and mass of R = 4R_⨀, M = 6M_⨀ has an average magnetic field of 1 × 10^-4 T. Calculate the strength of the magnetic field of the star when it evolves to a neutron star with the radius of 20 km.

parts.question: Calculate the strength of the magnetic field of the star when it evolves to a neutron star with radius 20 km.
parts.reference: Magnetic flux conservation: B * R^2 = B_ns * R_ns^2. B_ns = B * (R / R_ns)^2 = 1 * 10^-4 * ((4 * 6.96 * 10^5 km) / 20 km)^2 = 1.93 * 10^8 T.

tasks.title: Neutrino number density for dark matter
tasks.statement: Assume the mass of neutrinos is m_ν = 10^-5 m_e. Calculate the number density of neutrinos (n_ν) needed to compensate the dark matter of the universe. Assume the universe is flat and 25 % of its mass is dark matter. Hint: Take the classical total energy equal to zero

parts.question: Calculate the number density of neutrinos n_ν needed to compensate 25% dark matter in a flat universe.
parts.reference: Critical density rho_c = 3H^2 / (8pi G) = 1.1 * 10^-26 kg/m^3. Dark matter density rho_DM = 0.25 * rho_c = 3 * 10^-27 kg/m^3. n_ν = rho_DM / m_ν = 3 * 10^5 m^-3.

tasks.title: Earth orbit radius increase due to Sun mass loss
tasks.statement: Calculate how much the radius of the Earth’s orbit increases as a result of the Sun losing mass due to the thermo-nuclear reactions in its center in 100 years. Assume the Earth’s orbit remains circular during this period.

parts.question: Calculate the increase in the Earth's orbit radius in 100 years due to solar mass loss.
parts.reference: Solar luminosity L_sun = 3.83 * 10^26 W, mass loss rate dM/dt = -L_sun / c^2 = -4.26 * 10^9 kg/s. Angular momentum conservation M * r^2 * omega = const => dr/r = -dM/M => dr = -r * (dM/M). In 100 years, dr = 1.01 m.

tasks.title: Mars-Sun distance in Copernicus time
tasks.statement: Assume that you are living in the time of Copernicus and do not know anything about Kepler's laws. You might calculate Mars-Sun distance in the same way as he did. After accepting the revolutionary belief that all the planets are orbiting around the Sun, not around the Earth, you measure that the orbital period of Mars is 687 days, then you observe that 106 days after opposition of Mars, the planet appears in quadrature. Calculate Mars-Sun distance in astronomical unit (AU).

parts.question: Calculate Mars-Sun distance in AU using Copernicus method with given periods and quadrature time.
parts.reference: Angle of Earth in 106 days: (106 / 365.26) * 360 = 104.5°. Angle of Mars: (106 / 687) * 360 = 55.5°. Angle between Earth and Mars from Sun = 104.5° - 55.5° = 49.0°. In quadrature, cos(49°) = 1 / r_Mars => r_Mars = 1 / cos(49°) = 1.52 AU.

tasks.title: Satellite distance from Earth center
tasks.statement: A satellite is orbiting around the Earth in a circular orbit in the plane of the equator. An observer in Tehran at the latitude of φ = 35.6° observes that the satellite has a zenith angle of z = 46.0°, when it transits the local meridian. Calculate the distance of the satellite from the center of the Earth (in the Earth radius unit).

parts.question: Calculate the distance of the satellite from the center of the Earth in Earth radius units.
parts.reference: Angle EOS = 90 - phi = 54.4°. Zenith angle z = 46.0°. Angle ES_sat = 180 - z = 134°. Using sine rule in triangle EOS: r_sat / R_E = sin(54.4°) / sin(134°) = 3.98.

tasks.title: Eclipsing binary light variation
tasks.statement: An eclipsing close binary system consists of two giant stars with the same sizes. As a result of mutual gravitational force, stars are deformed from perfect sphere to the prolate spheroid with a = 2b, where a and b are semi-major and semi-minor axes (the major axes are always co-linear). The inclination of the orbital plane to the plane of sky is 90°. Calculate the amplitude of light variation in magnitude (Δm) as a result of the orbital motion of two stars. Ignore temperature variation due to tidal deformation and limb darkening on the surface of the stars. Hint: A prolate spheroid is a geometrical shape made by rotating of an ellipse around its major axis, like rugby ball or melon.

parts.question: Calculate the amplitude of light variation in magnitude (Δm) for the binary system.
parts.reference: When major axes are perpendicular to line of sight, projected area is proportional to b * a. When aligned with line of sight, projected area is proportional to b^2. Delta m = -2.5 * log(A_max / A_min) = -2.5 * log((b*a) / b^2) = -2.5 * log(a/b) = -2.5 * log(2) = -0.75 (or amplitude 0.75 magnitude).
